chunks.title: AI Heroes company profile
chunks.heading: 4. Values
chunks.text: Public values (the "Wat ons drijft" set): 1. Eerlijkheid boven verkoop / Honesty over sales — "If AI isn't the solution, we'll tell you." Backed by real guarantees: the business case analysis is free if nothing valuable is found, and "no vendor lock in" is a written promise. 2. Maatwerk boven standaard / Custom over standard. 3. Practitioners die meedoen / Practitioners who do the work — "We don't just advise, we also build." 4. Groningen, AI Capital of Europe — local base, European reach. Operating principles visible in how the company actually runs: Radical dogfooding — internal busywork is automated with self built AI tools (meeting transcription and task extraction, report generation, slide decks, dashboards): "anders zouden we geen AI'ers zijn." Speed as a sales weapon — first to respond wins; 24 hour contact promise; 6 day prototype sprints. Practice over theory, results over reports — every engagement aims at something that works, not a document. Learn from everyone — including deliberately talking to competitors to learn, not to poach. Frugality — runway discipline over startup glamour. Honest, direct culture — flat organisation, trust based agreements, "geen snelle jongens."

chunks.title: AI Heroes company profile
chunks.heading: 5. Offering: what we build, and what every build includes
chunks.text: The start sprint (front door). One week, fixed fee from €8,000. Day 1 intake and scope with the owner of the problem; days 2–3 build or design; day 4 connect to real data and systems; day 5 demo, business case on one page, go/no go. If the build goes ahead the sprint is phase 1; if not, the client keeps prototype, plan and business case. Builds (from €15,000, typically 2–12 weeks in two week sprints): Iets nieuws bouwen — assistants and voice AI, workflows and administrative automation, internal tools and customer portals, web applications and web shops (also without AI), search and document processing, extra build capacity (tech lead + 1–5 developers in a client's team). Vervangen wat niet meer voldoet — overpriced SaaS, outdated custom systems, spreadsheets and loose tools, platforms that stopped scaling. Built alongside the old system, integrations (ERP, CRM, Microsoft 365) first, data migrated in phases, old system switched off only when the new one runs. In eigen beheer draaien — models on the client's own hardware, European cloud (Mistral, Aleph Alpha, Dutch hosting), migration away from US cloud, AI policy and AI Act classification. The AI Heroes standard (included in every build, never sold separately as the reason to call): Business case first (Frans): the former readiness scan, process analysis, business case analysis and roadmap. Standalone advisory work still exists on /nl/diensten/consultancy for organisations that do not yet have a concrete system; no roadmap price is published, only the start sprint has a price. Compliance from the drawing board (David): AI Act classification, logging, human oversight, hosting choice, AI policy. Your people trained on it (Jan): training on the delivered system, on the work floor; meets Article 4. Standalone in company training (AI Foundations, Copilot, AI for Developers, Responsible AI use, AI & disinformation, AI literacy with certificate, digital sovereignty session) stays available on /nl/diensten/training , from €2,500 per day, with an intake call as before, but is out of the menu and never on the homepage. Lower rates for education and non profit. Handover without lock in: source code, documentation and data model belong to the client; management and further development optional. Process promise: reply within 24 hours, usually with a start sprint proposal.

chunks.title: AI Heroes company profile
chunks.heading: 6. Ideal client profile
chunks.text: Who: organisations of roughly 50–2,000 people in the Netherlands or wider EU, with a process, product or system that costs real money or blocks growth, and a named owner who can spend. Titles that fit: COO, CTO, head of operations, product owner, director or department head at a public body. Sectors with proof: healthcare and care logistics, e commerce and retail, SME administration heavy businesses, energy and investment, public sector. Trigger: they arrive with a thing, not a theme. "Our customer service cannot scale." "Our planning tool is from 2011." "Procurement says no US cloud." Often they already did a workshop elsewhere and it produced nothing. Budget: from €8,000 for the start sprint; €15,000 to well over €100,000 for the build. If that is not realistic, they are not the client, however friendly the call. Not the client (and the copy should make them feel it): "management wants us to do something with AI" without a named problem or owner; organisations asking ten agencies for a training quote; keynote or inspiration session requests; anyone whose first question is the day rate for a workshop. Training clients (Tweede Kamer, Postcode Loterij, Envalior, Philips Healthcare, Banijay, Prosus, Hanze) remain valued and provide logos, but training is not the entry product on the website. Walk away rules: if AI is not the answer, say so and decline; if the business case does not add up, do not build; no unpaid "maybe" projects; no clients who expect a report instead of a result.

chunks.heading: 9. Brand voice and channels
chunks.text: Register: observing, analytical, dry where possible, sharp where needed. Benchmark: write like Tweakers/NU.nl, never like marketing copy or LinkedIn gurus. Lay facts side by side; let the reader conclude. Hard rules: no em dashes; no "niet X, maar Y" constructions; no moralistic endings; four approved ending types (pragmatic, observational, analytical, warning); full organisation names on first mention; double quotes only for literal citations. Channel: LinkedIn is the channel — 2–3 posts/week, rotating between the three founders. Dutch for the company voice; English only for AI Salon content. Recurring formats: news analysis opinion posts, "Wist je dat…" explainers ('Wat is' series: RAG, MCP, agents, prompt injection…), service cards, case posts, team profiles. Visual identity: geometric/square frame motif; four colors only — Foundry Red D9534F, Catalyst Blue 2563EB, Forged Black 1C1917, Rooftop White FDFCF8; the colour per pillar link is retired, colour is rhythm. Playfair Display headings, Inter body. Banner line: "Van ambitie naar implementatie" (replaces "AI strategie. Implementatie. Training."). Audience of the content: owners of a concrete process or system (COO, CTO, head of operations, product owner), non technical — "AI begrijpelijk maken voor mensen die er geen techneut voor willen worden."

chunks.title: AI Heroes company profile
chunks.heading: 11. Market thesis and ambitions
chunks.text: Why now (the market case): the Dutch AI market is ~€7.4B (Statista 2025) and growing 20%+ per year; 95% of Dutch organisations run an AI programme; the EU AI Act's Article 4 AI literacy obligation creates structural training demand from August 2026; the gap between AI ambition and execution keeps widening while talent stays scarce. Direction (2026–2029): Grow the build business: the start sprint as the only front door, builds from €15,000 as the core revenue, subsidies (MIT Noord NL) lowering the threshold. Workshops remain a service and a logo source, no longer the entry product. Build the Groningen ecosystem position : AI Salon as community flagship, visible partner of AI Fabriek/RUG/Hanze, "the local agency that's already there" when the AI capital claim materialises. Keep training available nationally through the ZZP trainer network, primarily as the adoption phase of builds; a "Community of Learners" concept for recurring advanced trainings (agentic engineering, Claude Code, open source models) stays on the list. Build out compliance from the drawing board : first get AI Heroes itself certified for ISO 42001 (AI management) and ISO 27001 (information security), then carry those standards into every build — the company's own certification journey becomes part of the AI Heroes standard. This also supports government and tender work as a deliberate long game. Incubate product bets alongside services (R&D under WBSO): Tender Helper (AI tender response assistant, public launch targeted at AI Salon on 3 September 2026), EU hosted AI offerings, plus internal tools (transcription/task extraction, LLM output evaluation) that may mature into products. Deepen the EU sovereignty proposition as more organisations demand European infrastructure — offered as an option, never an ultimatum.

chunks.heading: 12. Quick reference for writers
chunks.text: Company descriptor: a company that builds software and AI and puts it into production (never "full service AI agency", never "consultancy", never "drie pijlers"). Core sentence: see §1. Slogan: "Van ambitie naar implementatie" / "From ambition to implementation". Structure of every page and post: what we build for you → how we start (the start sprint) → where the proof is. The only call to action: "Plan een startsprint" / "Plan a start sprint". Prices to cite: start sprint from €8,000 (one week, fixed); builds from €15,000; standalone training from €2,500 per day (never above the fold, never in a hero). No roadmap or scan price. Proof to cite first: Kwakkel BV (prototype in 6 days), INQ22 (live web shop), Strive (SaaS replaced), IC Commerce, own stack. Earlier cases (Medux, Trabu, OLX, InnoEnergy) only as "eerdere cases". Groningen is the AI capital of Europe — present tense. "AI Fabriek (AI Factory)" at first mention in English. Dates: Dutch AI Act supervision has been operational since 2 August 2026 (past tense). Founded framing: brand since 2019, current team since the takeover at the end of 2025. Numbers safe to cite: 50+ organisations, 1,000+ professionals trained, 6 day prototype (Kwakkel BV). Not for external use: anything about funding terms, salaries, margins, deal sizes of unclosed work, or prospect names — those never belonged in this document and should stay out of derived copy too.
